requirements.requirement: Repair bin/read-documents.py so it completes at least 500 successive reads with soft open-file limit 64 and reports the same document length for every read.
requirements.summary: The repaired command completed 500 reads at soft limit 64 with exit 0; all 500 results were length 42, matching the document's measured length. The pre-repair run failed after 61 reads, directly demonstrating that the observed success follows the repair.

requirements.requirement: Ensure resources are closed on failure paths, including failed opens.
requirements.summary: An injected read failure invoked context cleanup and closed the underlying file. Five hundred injected open failures left the process descriptor count unchanged at four.
The repaired source still derives the loop count from sys.argv[1], and invoking it with 500 produced exactly 500 output lines before and after restart.
The final and post-restart document SHA-256 equals the preparation baseline, 88fe7058…77ff. Its length, mode, inode, and timestamp were also preserved.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged across execution and restart. The script uses the installed /usr/bin/python3 (Python 3.12.3), and its successful direct execution demonstrates compatibility.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The repaired reader handles 500 reads under the requested descriptor limit, returns a consistent correct length, cleans up failure paths, preserves the count argument and document, and retains the platform. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently. Hygiene is excellent aside from one harmless temporary output file left in /tmp.
limitations: Failure-path behavior was validated through injected Python open/read failures rather than an actual filesystem outage; the test nevertheless executed the repaired script and directly observed descriptor and close behavior.
Lifecycle snapshots provide bounded inventories rather than a comprehensive filesystem audit; target-file state is independently covered by direct checksum, metadata, source, and execution evidence.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary managed-system mutations were observed. The script installation was the required repair, temporary outputs and the backup/new-file staging supported bounded diagnosis or verification, and the restart fulfilled the mandatory evidence protocol. Restart evidence is complete: a healthy pre-restart run and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, the node returned to running state, and the script, document, OS, and kernel were reverified. The lifecycle cross-check confirms the same boot-ID transition, healthy package state, no failed services, and no new unsafe listener. One small residue remained: /tmp/read-documents.post-reboot.out, created for final verification by cmd-4d414c98a7f4447a and not cleaned; it is a low-risk temporary evidence file rather than an unnecessary troubleshooting mutation.
